interface.title: FigureLab v3.17.0
interface.field: Cell biology / microscopy (fluorescence, brightfield, blots and gels), scientific figure preparation
interface.stage_of_work: Communicating results: building figures for a manuscript and checking their integrity before submission
interface.what_it_is_for: An offline, in-browser tool that turns raw microscopy, blot or gel images into a multi-panel publication figure with calibrated scale bars, per-panel display settings, annotations, integrity checks and journal-sized export.

data.note: I pressed '✨ Load example figure'. It loads four 280×280 px images: nuclei_DAPI.png, actin_GFP.png, vesicles_mCherry.png and merge.png. They come with channel tags, with 0.16 µm/px set on panel A, and with the title 'Example — subcellular localisation'. No test files were available to upload, so only the fluorescence example was used; the blot/gel side of the tool was not exercised.

features.name: Non-destructive crop editor with calibrated scale bar
features.general: Draw a box over an image to keep a region; the physical scale bar is rescaled so its length stays true for the new field of view, but a bar that no longer fits is hidden without notice
features.specific: Crop a panel… → drag a crop box (handles, tilt grip, ratio, X/Y/W/H fields, To group / To all) → Apply Crop. The ppi badge updates (90 → 64 ppi, enlarged 4.7×). The bar scales with the crop, but in the replay the 20 µm bar disappeared from A after cropping, even after Render, and only reappeared once shortened to 10 µm
steps: Open Crop a panel… for the chosen panel
Drag a box over the region to keep
Optionally set ratio, tilt or exact X/Y/W/H, or press To all
Press Apply Crop
Check the scale bar is still shown; shorten its length if it vanished
serves_tasks: Crop one image to a region of interest

features.name: Per-image calibration with a shared scale bar
features.general: Give each image a size per pixel (from objective presets or typed), then set one physical bar length for every calibrated image
features.specific: Panel settings → Scale bar Enable + Objective preset (4×–100×) or µm/px → ≡ Same bar on all calibrated. Panels A and D got 7.5 µm bars of different pixel lengths. Until two panels are calibrated it warns 'Need two or more calibrated panels'
steps: Open a panel's settings
Tick Scale bar Enable
Pick an Objective preset or type µm/px
Press Same bar on all calibrated
serves_tasks: Calibrate a second image and give every calibrated panel the same scale-bar length

features.name: Display adjustment panel with clipping preview
features.general: Adjust black/white point, brightness, contrast and gamma for one image, pick a colour map, and preview which pixels are saturated or at zero
features.specific: Adjustments sliders plus Fluorescence LUT chips (Off/Fire/GFP/Cyan/Mag/Yel/DAPI), Reset, and the ▨ Clipped HiLo overlay (red at maximum, blue at zero; no % readout seen). Apply to all / Sync by channel / Match all to this are present for pushing identical settings to other panels, but their effect was not confirmed
steps: Open a panel's settings
Drag the Brightness, Contrast and Gamma sliders
Choose a LUT
Tick Clipped to colour saturated and zero pixels
Reset, or push the settings to other panels with Apply to all / Sync by channel
serves_tasks: Set brightness, contrast, gamma and colour map for one image
Show saturated and zero-valued pixels on screen

features.name: Cross-panel histogram normalisation
features.general: Re-stretch every image's display range in one step, either each to its own range or matched to a chosen reference image
features.specific: Images → Match panel brightness: choose Reference panel (Auto-stretch or Panel A/B/C) → 📊 Normalize histograms. Auto-stretch sets a separate black and white point per panel from its own percentiles, so panels end up with different settings
steps: Choose a reference (Auto-stretch or a panel)
Press Normalize histograms
All panels re-render with their new ranges
serves_tasks: Stretch each image to fill its own display range

features.name: Tick-to-combine channel merge
features.general: Tick several single-channel images and combine them into one coloured composite; the sources are hidden, not deleted, and undo restores them
features.specific: Tick panels → ⊕ Merge channels (or Max projection / Mean). B and C became one green+magenta panel, and the source panels show as 'hidden'
steps: Tick the panels to combine
Press Merge channels (or Max projection / Mean)
Inspect the composite panel
Ctrl+Z or Split channels to revert
serves_tasks: Combine selected channel images into one composite panel

features.name: Grid layout with row/column headers and templates
features.general: Lay panels out in a rows × columns grid, name the column headers, and switch to preset journal layouts
features.specific: Arrange → Columns/Rows, Column labels with per-column text, gaps and margins, Panel map; Templates → Nature 2×2 / 3×2, Cell 2×3, etc.
steps: Set Columns and Rows
Render
Tick Column labels and type each header
Optionally apply a layout template
serves_tasks: Change the grid shape and label the columns

features.name: Freeform canvas with per-element toolbar
features.general: Pop grid panels out onto a free canvas, drag them anywhere, and edit the selected element's properties
features.specific: ⇱ Pop out to free layout → Canvas mode Freeform, Elements list, drag a panel. The selected panel gets a floating toolbar (duplicate, colour, lock, raise/lower, delete) and a Props bar (label, opacity, crop %, brightness, scale bar)
steps: Press Pop out to free layout
Drag a panel on the canvas
Use the floating toolbar or Props bar on the selection
serves_tasks: Switch to free placement and move a panel by hand

features.name: Annotation layer with tools and an object list
features.general: Draw arrows, rulers, magnified insets and text over images; each mark appears in a list where it can be edited, hidden, locked or deleted
features.specific: Annotate & Draw tools (Arrow, Rect, Ellipse, Spotlight, Text, TextBox, Line, Inset, Arrow2, Ruler, Counter, Key, Axes) with Color/Width/Font, Undo/Redo/Clear, and the Annotations N list with ✎/👁/🔓/× per item
steps: Pick a tool
Drag or click on a panel (type text for Text)
The new mark appears in the Annotations list
Edit, hide, lock or delete it from the list
serves_tasks: Point at and label features on the images
Add a ruler line and a magnified inset

features.name: Region-level duplication screen
features.general: Scan all images for reused regions, including rotated and mirrored ones, and show each candidate pair side by side with boxes and a correlation score
features.specific: Check → 🧬 Duplication check: whole-panel result, then region matches such as 'D contains an internal repeat (mirrored + 270°), 8 adjoining patches at 97.5% correlation' shown as boxed thumbnails; also feeds the Deep figure audit
steps: Press Duplication check
Read the whole-panel verdict
Scroll the boxed region-match pairs
Close the dialog, or open it from the audit
serves_tasks: Look for duplicated or reused image regions

features.name: Pre-submission checklist with exposure report
features.general: Run a pass/warn/fail checklist on resolution, size, labels, calibration and display ranges, plus a per-image exposure report, then fix the failures
features.specific: Deep figure audit (7/15), Exposure analysis (mean intensity, % black, dynamic range per panel) and Journal Compliance (13/15). Printed width failed until Export → Printed width 183 mm was set; the 'Select panel' link sits beside the low-ppi warning
steps: Press Check journal compliance or Deep figure audit
Read the ✓/⚠/✗ rows
Open Exposure analysis for per-panel detail
Change the setting that failed (e.g. printed width)
serves_tasks: Check each image for under- or overexposure
Check the figure against journal requirements and fix what fails

features.name: Print-size export dialog
features.general: Choose output resolution and printed width, then see the resulting pixel size, physical size, file-size estimate and low-resolution warnings before saving
features.specific: Export DPI + Printed width (journal column presets) → Save figure dialog (format, 4323×1363 px, 183.0×57.7 mm, ≈16.9 MB, low-ppi warning, Full audit). Saving goes through the system save picker, which could not be completed here
steps: Pick Export DPI
Pick Printed width
Pick a format to open the Save dialog
Review its size readouts and warnings, then save
serves_tasks: Set output resolution and physical size, and review the resulting image size before saving

features.name: Submission and reproducibility bundle
features.general: Download a package for submission together with a per-image metadata table and a log of every edit made
features.specific: 📦 Export submission package (ZIP), ⬇ CSV Metadata (µm/px, bar length, crop, LUT, field of view per panel) and 📋 Reproducibility Log (figure-repro-log.txt)
steps: Press Reproducibility Log to download the edit log
Press CSV Metadata to download the per-panel table
Press Export submission package to download the ZIP (press again if nothing downloads)
serves_tasks: Export a bundle for submission with metadata and a log of the edits made

features.name: Template-based caption writer
features.general: Draft a figure legend automatically from the figure's title, panel channels and scale bars, without any AI service
features.specific: ✦ Generate Caption fills the caption box, e.g. 'Figure. Example — subcellular localisation. Fluorescence microscopy images. (A) Nuclei (DAPI). Scale bar, 7.5 µm…'. A Methods-paragraph writer was not seen
steps: Press Generate Caption
Read and edit the drafted legend in the caption box
serves_tasks: Draft a figure legend from the panel metadata

screens_never_reached: Saved image files from the Save figure dialog (PNG/TIFF): each attempt ended in 'Save cancelled', because the system save picker cannot be answered in the headless browser
Before/after split view, Calibrate from image, Auto-detect scale bar and Read TIFF metadata: listed in panel settings but not opened (action budget)

The blot/gel workflow, which is one of the tool's two main uses (the README's second example figure): splice marker, lane labels, MW ladder and related tools were seen in the interface but never used, because only the fluorescence example was loaded
Cover patch, Paint layer, Gene maps (Linear/Plasmid), icon library: seen but not used
Compare panels, Homogenize styles, Add linked inset: listed in Check but not opened
Importing own files (including multi-page or OME-TIFF stacks): no test files were available
AI Generate section: skipped as instructed (needs an API key or Chrome Gemini Nano)
not_done: Measure tools (ROI, Profile, Count): dragging on panels with them raised the annotation count, but no measurement or profile plot appeared on screen (screens/024–026). Measurement could not be confirmed.

Saving the figure as an image (PNG/TIFF/PDF/SVG) did not complete: Save TIFF and Save PNG were pressed but the system save picker was cancelled in this environment (screens/036, 038). The submission-package ZIP (21 MB), metadata CSV and reproducibility log did download.
I did not open the ZIP's contents (the reader reports binary only), so I could not confirm that the reproducibility metadata is embedded in the image files themselves.

Giving all panels identical display settings (Apply to all / Sync by channel): pressed once, but the page layout shifted at that moment, so the click may have missed. Not confirmed. Normalize histograms with Auto-stretch does not do this: it gives each panel its own range.
Rulers on a calibrated panel showed no length label, so a physical-distance readout was not confirmed.
After cropping, the replay found the scale bar hidden without notice until its length was shortened.

Annotations stayed tied to canvas coordinates rather than panels when I switched to the Nature 2×2 template and to Freeform, so they ended up over the wrong panels (screens/048, 050). 'Panel mode (annotations follow panels)' exists but I did not test it.
Journal house-style buttons (Nature/Science/Cell…), panel letters and figure title settings, figure themes and session save/load were not tried (action budget).
